title: kith-chat: Message/set create
description:
What: Implement Message/set create JmapHandler in kith-chat crate — owner sends a message, optimistic return with deliveryState=pending, outbox enqueue.

Algorithm:
1. Deserialize args: { accountId, create: Map<String, Value> }.
2. Verify accountId == 'a-self'.
3. For each create entry (client_id → fields):
   a. Extract required: chatId (String), body (String), bodyType (String, default 'text/plain'). Optional: replyTo (String), sentAt (String).
   b. Validate body.len() <= 65536 bytes at parse time — BEFORE any lock acquisition.
   c. Validate bodyType in ['text/plain', 'text/markdown']; else notCreated/invalidArguments.
   d. Acquire store lock.
   e. Validate chatId exists: store.chats().get(chat_id)?; if None → notCreated/notFound.
   f. Validate replyTo if present: store.messages().get(reply_to_id)?; verify msg.chat_id == chat_id; else notCreated/invalidArguments.
   g. Generate ULID for message ID: ulid::Ulid::new().to_string().
   h. received_at_unix = now (SystemTime::now()).
   i. store.messages().insert(id, chat_id, 'self', body, body_type, sent_at_peer, received_at_unix, DeliveryState::Pending, reply_to)?
   j. store.chats().update_last_message_at(chat_id, received_at_unix)?
   k. Get recipients: SELECT peer_user_id, peer_mailbox_host FROM chat_members JOIN contacts WHERE chat_id=? AND peer_user_id != owner_id.
   l. For each recipient: store.outbox().enqueue(msg_id, peer_user_id, peer_mailbox_host, now_unix)?
   m. Release store lock.
   n. Add message to created map.
4. Return { accountId, oldState, created, notCreated, newState }.

Defensive programming rules:
- body.len() check is byte count (not char count) — enforce BEFORE acquiring store lock.
- bodyType whitelist check before any DB write.
- chatId validated against DB (must exist) before message insert.
- replyTo validated: must exist AND must be in same chatId; cross-chat replyTo → invalidArguments.
- sentAt: store as-is from client; NEVER used for ordering (receivedAt is authoritative).
- ULID generated server-side; never trust client-supplied message ID.
- All DB writes in one lock acquisition per create entry (atomic within one message).
- Outbox enqueue happens inside same lock guard as message insert.
- KithError from any store call → notCreated[client_id] = server_fail (do not abort other creates).

Agent team:
- Agent R: Read kith-store/src/message.rs (insert signature), kith-store/src/outbox.rs (enqueue), kith-store/src/chat.rs (get, update_last_message_at), kith-core/src/message.rs (DeliveryState), ulid crate usage in workspace.
- Agent I: Implement MessageSetCreateHandler in kith-chat/src/message.rs.
- Agent T: Tests using in-memory store, hand-crafted expected JMAP response. Oracle: JMAP field names from RFC 8620 §5.3 + kith-core serde attrs.
- Agent V: cargo test -p kith-chat && clippy && fmt.

Tests:
- Message/set create valid → created.m0 has id (ULID), deliveryState='pending', body echoed
- Message/set create body > 65536 bytes → notCreated/invalidArguments (before any DB write)
- Message/set create unknown chatId → notCreated/notFound
- Message/set create valid replyTo → created successfully
- Message/set create replyTo from different chat → notCreated/invalidArguments
- After create: outbox has entry for recipient
